problem_framing.reason: A1 separates the objective (whether to invest, on mid-1962 evidence) from the suggested solution. It lists real alternatives: deepen the dealer offer, no expansion, or a different customer group. It also names the independent-dealer constraint. It does not correct a false premise or surface a non-obvious constraint. The euro-denominated €20,000 budget is anachronistic for 1962 and is not in the case packet. If the protocol did not supply it, it is an invented number and would cap this dimension at 1. Scored 2 on the assumption that it is a protocol test budget.

causal_mechanism.reason: T1 names a benefit (status and convenience) and a value-capture route. The behaviour-change premise 'homeowners already owned Deere tractors for farming' is asserted without any source. The value-capture route, direct-to-consumer sales that bypass dealers, is unsupported and conflicts with the dealer-model constraint recorded in A1. The chain from behaviour change to captured value is therefore not credibly traced.

distinct_theories.reason: T1 and T2 are near-identical rewordings. They share the same customer (homeowners), the same benefits text, the same value capture (premium pricing plus direct-to-consumer sales) and an identical brand-perception prediction. They differ mainly in 'status' versus 'ease of use' and do not imply different products, customers or channels.

assumptions_predictions.reason: The predictions are observable: survey willingness to pay, regional sales concentration and brand surveys. However, the premium is benchmarked against a 'standard farm tractor', which is an incoherent comparison. The 20% and 15% thresholds are untested assumptions. The shared brand prediction cannot separate the theories, so failure would not clearly put either theory in trouble.

evidence_judgement.reason: Source classes are mislabelled. deere-wheelhorse-demand, deere-green-venture and deere-wiki-dealers are verified_observation in the dossier but are called independent_study in A14, A16 and A17. A14 marks the Wheel Horse demand quote as supporting T1's premium/status theory, although the source says the tractors were found 'rather inexpensive', which cuts against a premium status play. The quote also concerns a competitor's market and has no stated date or place. A12 and A17 rely on post-mid-1962 outcomes (1963 production; the company's decision to enter the market), breaching the frame's own date constraint in A1. A17 treats the company's decision as support for homeowner demand. The 'does not show' notes are present but generic and never mention date, place or fit with the customer group.

seeking_challenge.reason: A13 runs one search against T1. The disconfirming element it returned (consumers valued garden tractors as inexpensive) was then recorded as support in A14 rather than reported fairly. No challenge was run against T2.

experiment_design.reason: The run stopped at A18 before any test was proposed or declined.

revision.reason: A scheduled update was applicable but was never delivered, and the run stopped at A18.

recommendation.reason: The investigation stopped before a recommendation because of repeated errors.

red_flags.reason: The episode has no completed recommendation. Experiment design and revision were also never reached.
The source's emphasis on garden tractors being 'rather inexpensive' is presented as support for a premium-priced status-symbol theory. This misreads the source's meaning relative to the claim.
Deere's decision to enter the consumer market is treated as supporting homeowner demand and status motivation. A company action is not evidence of consumer demand.

Both theories assert, with no source, that 'homeowners already owned Deere tractors for farming'. Both also assert direct-to-consumer value capture with no source, conflicting with the dealer-model constraint in A1.
The run relies on hindsight: 1963 production and the company's later market entry are used as evidence for a mid-1962 decision, contrary to the frame's own pre-mid-1962 source constraint.
Source classes are mislabelled: dossier verified_observation sources are relabelled as independent_study.

judgment.screen_reason: Rejected. The episode is incomplete (stopped at A18 with no recommendation). It also contains a misread source counted as support (A14), a company decision treated as demand evidence (A17), hindsight reliance (A12, A17) and unsourced premises in the theories (A9, A10). Any one of these critical errors would disqualify the trajectory.
